A SmartKnob-style haptic dial built from breakout boards

Heat the pad and the pin together for two seconds. Feed solder into the joint, not onto the iron. Take the solder away first, then the iron.

Strip 3 mm, twist the strands, and tin the end before you solder it to a pad.

Unplug USB and disconnect any battery before you solder or change a wire. Work on a surface that does not burn, and wash your hands after handling solder.

Before you switch it on

  1. Look. Every joint is a shiny cone. No solder touches a neighbouring pad. No stray strands of wire.
  2. These must not beep. Set the multimeter to continuity and probe each pair. A beep means a short: find it before you plug in.
    VINGND3V3GND
  3. These must beep. Probe the two ends of every connection.
    VINController VIN · Motor driver VIN
    GNDController GND · Motor driver GND
    3V3Controller 3V3 · Motor driver VIO · Angle sensor VCC · Round display VCC
    UHController D26 · Motor driver UH
    ULController D25 · Motor driver UL
    VHController D27 · Motor driver VH
    VLController D13 · Motor driver VL
    WHController D14 · Motor driver WH
    WLController D4 · Motor driver WL
    MOTOR_UMotor driver U · Gimbal motor A
    MOTOR_VMotor driver V · Gimbal motor B
    MOTOR_WMotor driver W · Gimbal motor C
    GNDController GND.2 · Angle sensor GND · Round display GND
    MT_DATAController D19 · Angle sensor DO
    MT_CLOCKController TX2 · Angle sensor CLK
    MT_CSNController RX2 · Angle sensor CSN
    LCD_MOSIController D23 · Round display SDA
    LCD_SCLKController D18 · Round display SCL
    LCD_CSController D22 · Round display CS
    LCD_DCController D21 · Round display DC
    LCD_RSTController D15 · Round display RST
  4. Plug in. Nothing gets warm, nothing smells. If something does, unplug at once and go back to step 2.
  5. Flash the bring-up test. It reports every part it can find before you load the real firmware.pio run -e bringup -t upload && pio device monitor
30DREIE-WIRE-1

Dreie is built

Dreie is a motorized dial that fakes detents, springs and end stops with a brushless gimbal motor and a magnetic angle sensor, with a round screen riding inside the knob. It is the electronics of Scott Bezek's SmartKnob View rebuilt from off-the-shelf breakouts around a classic ESP32, so it runs the upstream SmartKnob firmware with a remapped pin list instead of needing the fine-pitch View PCBs. It is for an experienced hobbyist who wants to experiment with haptic feedback before committing to the full View build.
